newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: ING rates Slovak Slovnaft long-term buy.
newsitem.headline: ING rates Slovak Slovnaft long-term buy.

text.p: Shares of Slovakia's sole oil refiner Slovnaft a.s. are a long-term buy, an investor report issued by INB Barings said on Tuesday.
The report rated the shares as a long-term buy at the price of 997 crowns as of August 30. On Monday Slovnaft did not trade on the Bratislava Stock Exchange, after closing at 920 crowns on Friday.
"We remain buyers of Slovnaft for the long term, but short term investors should take profits ahead of expectations of full year results falling bellow market forecasts," the report said.
Slovnaft posted a pre-tax profit of 291.4 million crowns in the first six months of this year, compared to 2.25 billion for the same period in 1995.
The drop in profits resulted from a slowdown in output due to general maintenance of major production units and an increase in the world prices of crude oil.
The company has said that despite the lower first half result, it did not see reason for revising its forecast of around 2.4 billion crowns gross profit in 1996.
But ING Barings said it had cut its forecasts for Slovnaft's full year profit to around 1.2 billion crowns given the potential for higher financial costs and a weak market for petrochemicals.
"Management is still projecting a strong full year result but we are taking a cautious line," the report said.

It said that second half margins would be adversely affected by recent oil prices, and that despite an increase in prices of petrochemical products, these should remain well bellow the 1995 average level in the second half of this year.
The report added that Slovnaft's ongoing modernisation investment programme was also resulting in the steady growth of financial costs.

"Although we expect a much stronger operating result in the second half, we believe the full year result will not come close to last year's net profit of 1.768 billion crowns, giving significant potential for the full year result to disappoint," the report said.
